what_its_for: Flecainide is used to treat certain types of irregular heartbeats (arrhythmias). It helps your heart beat in a more normal, steady rhythm. Your doctor may prescribe it for conditions like atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, or other fast or irregular heart rhythms.
how_to_take: Take flecainide exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Take it at evenly spaced times throughout the day (usually every 12 hours) to keep a steady amount in your body. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablets unless your doctor says it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your heart condition, weight, and kidney function. Most adults start with 50 to 100 mg every 12 hours. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose if needed, up to a maximum of 400 mg per day. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can be dangerous.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is within 6 hours of the time you were supposed to take it. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store flecainide tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice, as it may affect how this medicine works in your body. Avoid taking over-the-counter medicines, herbal products, or supplements without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, especially antacids that contain milk of magnesia or Maalox, which can reduce how well flecainide works. Avoid smoking, as it can decrease the levels of flecainide in your blood. Limit alcohol, as it can affect your heart rhythm. Do not drive or use heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause dizziness or vision changes.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a new or worsening irregular heartbeat, very fast or pounding heartbeat, chest pain or tightness, sudden dizziness or fainting, shortness of breath, vision changes or seeing halos around lights, signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, unusual swelling in your legs or ankles, or if you feel like your heart medication is not working as well as it used to.
when_it_works: Flecainide begins working within a few hours of your first dose. However, it may take several days to a few weeks for your doctor to find the right dose and for you to feel the full benefit of the medication. Regular follow-up appointments and heart monitoring (EKG) are important to make sure the medicine is working safely and effectively for you.
special_populations: Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and may need a lower dose. Kidney or liver problems: If your kidneys or liver do not work well, your doctor will need to adjust your dose and monitor you more closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may pass into breast milk. Your doctor will help weigh the risks and benefits. Children: The use of flecainide in children should be closely supervised by a heart specialist (cardiologist).
